agreements – watch liveAndrew SparrowMon 23 Nov 2026 17.53 GMTFirst published on Mon 23 Nov 2026 09.15 GMTShareFrom 1h ago16.30 GMTBurnham says it would be 'unthinkable' for the UK to rejoin the EU without a referendumThe Conservative MP Bernard Jenkin asked Burnham if he agreed it would be “unthinkable” for a government to take the UK back into the EU with a referendum.

Burnham replied: “Yes, it would be unthinkable.”

Burnham has previously signalled that a referendum would be necessary, but this is his clearest commitment yet to not joining the EU without a referendum.

taking questions from MPs about his statement. In response to a question from Calum Miller (Lib Dem), Burnham said he was amazed the Conservatives were saying they will vote against the legislating implementing this legislation when they have not even seen the details.

5m ago17.50 GMTThe latest episode of the Guardian’s Politics Weekly UK podcast is out. Pippa Crerar has been speaking to the PM and she discussed with Kiran Stacey how Andy Burnham will get the public to accept an EU reset.

Read moreShare9m ago17.47 GMTGreens' Ellie Chowns says Burnham should set out pathway for rejoining EUEllie Chowns, the parliamentary leader of the Greens, told Burnham she welcomed the “shift in tone from the Labour benches” in recognising that “Brexit was disastrous”. She went on:

double quotation markSo can I ask him where will he set out the pathway to the truly brightest future for Britain, ie. to rejoin the EU?

Burnham said he would set out a bold plan for Britain next month.

19m ago17.36 GMTMunira Wilson (Lib Dem) asked if the deal agreed on Friday was contingent on the UK and the EU reaching a deal on tuition fees.

Burnham said Ursuala von der Leyen, the European Commission president, was clear on Friday that the deal on tuition fees was separate.

23m ago17.33 GMTRichard Tice, the Reform UK deputy leader, said this was a terrible deal. He said the youth mobility scheme would make it harder for Neets to find jobs. And he asked what Burnham would say to Jonathan Hinder, the Labour MP who told Newsnight last week that Labour’s strategy was in danger of making red wall voters think the government was treating them like thick, northern racists.

Burnham said he was confused by Reform Uk’s position because Nigel Farage was on record as saying Brexit had failed. He suggested he could not understand why Reform UK was not in favour of making the situation better.

30m ago17.26 GMTBurnham says EU deal won't override UK laws on animal fur productsRuth Jones (Lab) asked for an assurance that the deal would not negate UK legislation banning the import of some animal fur products.

double quotation markIt was a specific point of negotiation that all of our domestic controls over animal welfare were retained.

34m ago17.22 GMTKirsty Blackman (SNP) asked for an assurance that nothing in the deal would remove powers from devolved governments.

Burnham said the deal should be implementing with respect for the powers of the devolved goverments.

36m ago17.19 GMTBurnham reprimands Labour MP who accuses him of breaking Makerfield byelection promise over BrexitGraham Stringer (Lab) said Burnham fought extremism when he was mayor of Greater Manchester. He said Burnham, during the Makerfield byelection campaign, said “it would be wrong to reopen the debate on Europe because it would be divisive”. But Burnham did exactly that in Brussels, he said. He went on:

double quotation markThat leads to cynicism and a loss of trust in parliamentary democracy and where there is a loss of trust in parliamentary democracy, you get extremists.

Burnham rejected the claim he had gone back on what he told voters in Makerfield.

double quotation markIt was around the 10-year anniversary of the referendum, and I was talking about rerunning the referendum. I am not proposing at this moment to rerun the referendum …

I am somebody who does take care about what I say and stick to it …

I inherited that situation [the plans for the deal with the EU], and it was entirely in keeping with the manifesto [Stringer] was elected on, I was elected on, to develop that deal because we promised the public of Makerfield and the country to deliver closer ties with Europe. That is what this deal does.

And I don’t think it helps anybody for him to stand up and say that somehow I’ve somehow either broken that trust because I haven’t.

43m ago17.12 GMTHilary Benn, who was Northern Ireland secretary when Keir Starmer was PM, said he thought “working more closely together with our European friends and neighbours is absolutely in our country’s national interest”.

46m ago17.10 GMTEsther McVey (Con) said the government wanted to allow 50,000 young people from the EU to come to the UK under the youth mobility scheme, but ended up accepting 100,000. In a reference to this mini-row, she said Burnham’s time would be better spent “polishing up his negotiating skills rather than concentrating on the choreography of a dance routine of a TikTok influencer”.

Burnham said McVey’s question probably sounded better when she practised it in the mirror in her office.

52m ago17.03 GMTBurnham said deal should offer 'some reassurance' to UK car sector on Made in Europe, but final deal on this not yet agreedLayla Moran (Lib Dem) asked for an assurance that the proposed 10% tariff on electric vehicle (EV) exports to the UK would not be going ahead. And would the UK have to impose tariffs on Chinese EVs?

Burnham said he realised this was a vital issue for Moran’s constituents working at the Mini factory in Cowley. He went on:

double quotation markWe are doing all we can … And there is language in the agreement which I were pointed towards which should give her some reassurance.

But we have not reached a final conclusion yet.

Later Anneliese Dodds (Lab) also asked about EV tariffs.

Burnham said he should have said the Mini plant was in Dodds’ Oxford East constituency, not Moran’s Oxford West and Abingdon constituency.

double quotation markTo repeat, Made in Europe [the EU law that could penalise British EVs without the concessions the government is seeking] was not on the table as part of this negotiation. I put it on the table and we got it in the agreement. And that is good negotiation. And I hope it will turn into something meaningful for her constituents.
